meta.description: For property managers and landlords in Québec: Verikora reads the lease against the Civil Code of Québec, examines the pay stub as a file, and shows the exact line behind every finding.

landing.title: Read before you sign.
landing.lead: For property managers and landlords who screen applicants in Québec: drop the lease and the applicant's papers. Verikora verifies the documents and screens the file: it reads them against extraction matrices and technical templates, and shows you the exact line behind every finding.

status.label: Status
status.development: In development: sign-up is closed while we test it on real Québec leases.
status.preview: Dev preview: sign-up is closed, access by invitation.

hero.leaseCaption: One clause of the lease, lit
hero.findingCaption: What Verikora returns, with its source

what.title: What it does
what.lead: Three things, with nothing hidden behind them.
what.who: For property managers and landlords who screen applicants in Québec: a lease and a pay stub per file, several files a month. Tenants are welcome too: their first check is free. The registry checks (SOQUIJ, TAL, plumitif) are in preparation.
what.trust: By default, your account and your checks are kept in a database in Toronto, Canada, and seen by your account alone; your files can go to your own storage instead, when you choose it. Nothing is sold, shared or used to train a model.

line.title: The exact line behind every finding
line.text: Each finding names the rule, quotes the article of law and lights the sentence of the lease it rests on.

file.title: The PDF examined as a file
file.text: Producer, dates, successive saves: three levels (observed, unusual, inconsistent), never a « fake » stamp.

find.title: Find everything in a second
find.text: One word, and every document and every finding comes back, the passage in bold.

proof.title: One real check
proof.lead: A sample lease, checked in development and recorded as it came back. The rule, the line, the article of law, the run id and the date are the engine's answer, not typed by hand.
proof.figures: {rules} rules checked, {found} findings on this sample lease.

closing.title: One file, one answer.
closing.body: Sign in to check the files of your month. Visible to your account only.
closing.bodyIn: The files of your month are in your library, checked and seen by your account alone.

visual.caption: A real check, recorded as it came back

showcase.title: The app, as it is
showcase.lead: Three screens of Verikora, drawn with its own components on fictitious data. Nothing here is a screenshot.

findings.title: Every finding quotes its line
findings.text: The rule, the sentence of the lease it rests on, and the article of law, in the order to read them.
findings.summary: The report of a check: the verdict, then each finding with the quoted passage of the lease and its article.

screening.title: A screening the tenant agrees to
screening.text: The applicant sees the result first; a registry check that is not ready says so instead of guessing.
screening.summary: A screening result with the checks asked and, for each, its outcome: nothing to report, or not available yet.

owner.title: A report the owner can open
owner.text: A read-only page by link, with an expiry: the file's fingerprint, the findings and the run that produced them.
owner.summary: The owner's page: the document fingerprint, the findings with their articles, and the run id.

stage.title: Development version
stage.message: Data can be reset at any time. This is not a commercial offer yet.
